_comment: Declared CI timeouts, and the policy for deciding when they no longer match
This repo has no numeric quality thresholds to tune. Coverage is a recorded
decision rather than a percentage (tests/test-coverage.sh explains why), and
the shellcheck bar is zero output, which is not a dial. What genuinely
drifts here is job duration: the image build tracks the size and layer count
of an upstream base this repo does not control, so a timeout that was
generous when it was written can quietly become tight.
The statistic is the MAXIMUM observed duration, not a percentile. A timeout
has to cover the worst run, not the typical one -- a p95 that fits tells you
nothing about the 1-in-20 run that gets killed at the cap.
Keep timeout_minutes in step with the workflow files. The workflow reports a
mismatch it cannot see; it reads the numbers here, not the YAML.

_at_risk_ratio: Fail when the slowest recent run exceeds this fraction of the timeout.
At 0.75 a job that has grown to three quarters of its cap is reported
while there is still room to react, rather than after the first run dies.
_loose_ratio: Advisory only, never a failure. A timeout more than five times the
slowest observed run is not harmful, it just means a hung job burns that
long before the runner reclaims it.

jobs.note: Scales with the upstream Aurora base; the one entry here that is expected to move.
Two skopeo inspects and a git push. 15 matches nightly-compliance.yml's Published image, which does the same kind of registry work.

This job. Its runtime scales with the length of the list above -- each entry costs two run listings plus up to 2 x sample_size job queries -- so it is the one job here whose drift this repo causes directly.

_untracked: Jobs that declare a timeout but are deliberately not sampled above. An
absent job is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, so the decision is
recorded as data rather than implied by omission, and
tests/test-auto-qa-tuning.sh requires every job in .github/workflows to
appear in exactly one of the two lists.

untracked.job: Read back merged agent pull requests
untracked.reason: Runs once a month, so a 20-run sample would span years and the row would read 'no successful runs sampled' for most of them. Its time is set by how many agent pull requests merged in the window (one gh call each); the 15-minute cap is a budget, not a measurement.

Duration is set by the model, not by this repo's code. The number would move on its own with no change here to explain it, which is the definition of a metric that trains people to ignore it. The 30-minute cap is a budget, not a measurement.

Runs only when someone labels an issue ai-fix-requested, so the sample is usually empty and the row would read 'no successful runs sampled' indefinitely. Bounded at 5 minutes for a handful of gh api calls.

untracked.job: Open or update the failure issue
untracked.reason: Its step runs only after another workflow has failed, so the sample is usually empty and the row would read 'no successful runs sampled' indefinitely. Bounded at 5 minutes for a handful of gh calls.
